title.value: Leishmania parasites exchange drug-resistance genes through extracellular vesicles
title.justification: The paper's content focuses on the exchange of drug-resistance genes among Leishmania parasites via extracellular vesicles, hence the title is descriptive of the main study.
title.quote: Douanne et al. demonstrate that extracellular vesicles (EVs) released by drug-resistant Leishmania are enriched in genomic regions containing drug-resistance genes.

extractions.description: This paper explores the mechanism by which Leishmania parasites exchange drug-resistance genes using extracellular vesicles (EVs). It investigates the DNA content of EVs derived from drug-resistant parasites and their role in horizontal gene transfer, leading to the propagation of drug-resistant subpopulations. The study demonstrates how EVs serve as carriers of genetic material that improves resilience and adaptability of the parasites in stressful environments.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper does not primarily focus on climate or ecological sustainable development themes, but rather on a biological study specific to microbial genetics and resistance.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Leishmania are eukaryotic parasites that have retained the ability to produce extracellular vesicles (EVs) through evolution.

primary_category.justification: Neither climate nor ecological sustainable development is the central theme of this paper, which focuses on medical parasitology and drug resistance.
primary_category.quote: Herein, we investigate the DNA content of EVs derived from drug-resistant parasites, as well as the EVs’ potential to act as shuttles for DNA transfer.

primary_sub_category.justification: There are no direct applications or discussions related to climate or ecological sustainable development in the paper's findings.
primary_sub_category.quote: Leishmania are eukaryotic parasites that have retained the ability to produce extracellular vesicles (EVs) through evolution.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper focuses on the genetic mechanisms of drug resistance in Leishmania parasites facilitated by extracellular vesicles.
new_primary_category.quote: Douanne et al. demonstrate that extracellular vesicles (EVs) released by drug-resistant Leishmania are enriched in genomic regions containing drug-resistance genes.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The study specifically investigates the role of extracellular vesicles in facilitating horizontal gene transfer among Leishmania parasites, contributing to drug resistance.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: We provide evidence that eukaryotic EVs function as efficient mediators in HGT, thereby facilitating the transmission of drug-resistance genes and increasing the fitness of cells when encountering stressful environments.
